title: fix(ui): stop showing unknown chat authors as the viewer
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Messages with no recorded author could borrow the signed-in viewer’s name and avatar. Reply previews and Markdown exports could repeat that false attribution, including for existing history.

## User Impact

Unattributed inputs now show **Message**, with **no avatar**. Recorded authors, qualified own/peer profiles, CLI/source labels, and alignment remain intact. Chat, replies, and exports use the same neutral wording.

This works for old records without rewriting stored messages, roles, provenance, permissions, or replay metadata. An older message that really was yours but never recorded its author also gets this neutral presentation; its author cannot safely be reconstructed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only a verified matching profile establishes that an input belongs to the viewer. The fix stays at the presentation boundary rather than inventing historical sender data. The general avatar helper still supports genuine local-user previews.

The revision also removes redundant coverage: the 344-line standalone browser suite is gone, its unique assertions extend the existing export suite, and the new renderer tests shrink from 238 to 111 lines. The complete PR is **180 additions / 35 deletions**, down from 610 / 31.

## Evidence

- **260 focused UI tests and 14 Talk-history tests passed**, covering the renderer, export, hydration, subagent presentation, and persisted Talk custody. The revised regression first failed on the previous implementation (four failures, two attribution controls passing).
- **11,350 UI/library tests exercised**: 11,349 passed on the broad run. The remaining test assumed an unattributed message had an avatar; its fixture now records an author so it still checks identity-gutter invalidation. All **24 tests in that suite then passed**. Production code did not change after the broad run.
- **34 Chromium E2E checks passed** across export attribution, slash commands, and attributed identity. Includes two signed-in viewers, clipboard/download parity, existing author presentation and responsive layouts. Both updated export cases failed on the prior PR revision and passed after the change.
- Full changed-check gate passed for the staged PR delta: affected test type graphs, UI types, formatting, lint, i18n, dead exports, and repository guards.
- CI exposed one additional Talk-export expectation of “You”; it now expects “Message” while preserving the real RPC/custody/reopen checks. All 14 local Talk tests pass; the test-only repair also passed its changed-check gate and independent P2 review. Required CI passed on exact replacement head `08dee0d5` in [run 36477767567, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36477767567). Attempt 1 had one unacquired self-hosted job; its targeted retry and dependent gate succeeded, without another source change.
- Independent AutoReview through P2: **scoped-clean**. A conditional source-only-avatar concern was checked against the unchanged classifier and dismissed: source-only groups cannot contain a sender or sender label.

<details>
<summary>Measured test cost</summary>

One-worker file test wall time (Vitest start/end span; compilation/startup excluded), using the canonical runner with --maxWorkers=1. No worker pin was added to the tests or CI config.

| Test file | Cases | One-worker seconds | CI seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| chat-message-attribution.test.ts | 6 | 0.013 | 0.074 |
| chat-message.test.ts | 207 | 1.814 | 8.454 |
| chat-message.subagent.test.ts | 3 | 0.091 | 0.452 |
| chat-pane-snapshot-hydration.test.ts | 7 | 0.491 | 0.965 |
| chat-transcript-invalidation.test.ts | 24 | 1.095 | 2.813 |
| export.test.ts | 13 | 0.003 | 0.018 |
| chat-export-attribution.e2e.test.ts | 2 | 8.949 | 5.841 |
| server.talk-consult-history.test.ts | 14 | 10.093 | 68.61 (previous failing shard, 8 cases) |

The UI measurement command completed in 19.26 s; the Talk command completed in 80.99 s including a 40.32 s cold compilation. The browser export file uses the existing one-worker serial E2E project. These are file test timings, not fabricated per-file shares of process startup.

The existing slash-command-ranking file only changes an export-label expectation; its unchanged seven-case flow took 16.047 s in the prior isolated browser run (bundled project), with CI cost 17.344 s. No cases were added.

The Talk suite keeps real RPC admission, transcript custody/publication, abort ownership, and SQLite reopen behavior; a renderer mock cannot prove those boundaries. This follow-up only changes its expected export heading, adding no test cases or setup. CI cost above 30 s is therefore retained rather than hiding or deleting the custody coverage. Browser export coverage needs the actual UI, download, and clipboard paths; it replaces the removed duplicate standalone suite.

CI values are from [run 36472563182, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36472563182), head `7c2805f8`: UI module diagnostic.duration (three workers with file sharding), and browser per-file summaries. They exclude queue/setup/collection time and are not a claim of a passing replacement-head run. Every listed UI/browser file passed. The separate Talk row records the prior failing shard, not passing evidence.

</details>

### Before this revision

![User with a person icon](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68d60611-f161-4845-b26d-aa482fb14811)

### After

![Message with no avatar; recorded authors unchanged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ef567bb-0985-4e06-b8a6-8bbfc31b2c97)

Actual Control UI with synthetic Gateway history; same 1280×900 viewport, light theme, content, and scroll position. Browser checks ran in an isolated Testbox; its lease was stopped. The screenshot and local results are separate from the exact-head CI result above.

Thanks @vyctorbrzezowski for the report, backward-compatibility requirement, and presentation direction.
